# Compact Fusion Reactor
The station runs on a compact fusion reactor. The reactor itself makes no electricity: it heats coolant gas, and a [color=orange]gas turbine[/color] turns that heat into power for the [color=orange]HV network[/color].
## The loop The coolant runs in a [bold]closed loop[/bold]:
[color=orange]reactor outlet[/color] → [color=lightblue]turbine inlet[/color] → turbine outlet → [color=cyan]radiators in space[/color] → [color=lightblue]reactor inlet[/color]
- The reactor and the turbine both move gas on their own. The loop needs no extra pump. - The radiators cool the turbine exhaust before it returns to the reactor. The colder the gas entering the reactor, the cooler the core runs. - The loop must [bold]close[/bold]. If the turbine exhaust has nowhere to go, its outlet fills up, the gas stops and the turbine makes nothing. Examine the turbine: it tells you when its outlet is full.
## Filling the loop Power depends on how much gas flows, not only on how hot it is. - Fill the loop to roughly [color=orange]3000–4500 kPa[/color] (measured on the cold side). At a few hundred kPa the turbine makes almost nothing and the core overheats at any real power. - Nitrogen works. Carbon dioxide, water vapour and nitrous oxide carry a little more heat per mole. Frezon carries far more. Tritium is a poor coolant. - The reactor window and the turbine show inlet and outlet pressure and the flow in mol/s. If the flow is 0, something in the loop is blocked or empty.
With a nitrogen loop at about 4500 kPa and the reactor at full power, the turbine gives roughly [bold]700 kW[/bold], and the core stays around 1000 K. At lower pressure the turbine gives about the same power, but the core runs much hotter.
The turbine takes 60% of the heat above room temperature out of the gas and turns 60% of that into electricity. The rest of the heat leaves through the radiators.
## Running the reactor - The containment field needs [color=orange]APC power[/color]. Without it the reactor winds down and the field weakens. - Insert a [color=cyan]fuel cassette[/color]. Cassettes are ordered from cargo. The cassette is locked in while the reactor runs. - The reactor needs power before the turbine makes any: start it from the SMES or batteries. - Set the power and press [bold]Start reactor[/bold]. Output rises gradually. Start at 30–50% and raise it while watching the core temperature. - Higher power burns fuel faster and heats the core faster. The core only stays cool if enough gas flows through it.
## Danger Above the safe core temperature the containment field starts to fail; the hotter the core, the faster it fails. Engineering is warned over the radio as the field weakens.
If the field reaches 0%, the reactor [color=red]breaches[/color]: an explosion, a burst of superheated gas, and an electromagnetic pulse that knocks out nearby electronics. The reactor is wrecked.
[bold]Shutting down always works.[/bold] Press Shut down, keep coolant flowing, and the core cools on its own.
## Turbine Gas hotter than the turbine can take wears down its blades. A turbine with wrecked blades makes no power until it is repaired with a [color=orange]welder[/color].
